description:
Definition of a channel within an org's substrate. Carries the channel's handle (the colon-pathed tree address), human-readable name, purpose statement, creator DID, and visibility class. ChannelDefs are listed inside the parent org's `tech.equanimi.secretariat.orgDoc` (hosted at the org's well-known service endpoint) and/or published as records to the org's `_org/channels` meta-queue when channels are created or modified. The handle is the unique key within an org; tree nesting is expressed as colon-pathed segments (e.g. `dommage-corporel:paris-cohort` is a child of `dommage-corporel`).

**v0.5 grammar (namespace-collapse).** Handles no longer carry a top-level `channel:` / `inbox:` / `area:` / `project:` namespace token. Form is bare `<segment>(:<segment>)*` — colons separate tree depth. The queue-root (`_self` vs `<org-alias>`) is carried by the envelope's `to` DID, not by the handle itself.

handle.description: The channel's handle, colon-pathed for tree nesting. Form (v0.5): `<segment>(:<segment>)*` where each segment matches `[a-z_][a-z0-9_-]*`. Tree depth = colon depth (e.g. `dommage-corporel:paris-cohort`). No top-level `channel:` / `inbox:` / `area:` / `project:` namespace prefix — the queue-root (`_self` vs `<org-alias>`) is carried by the envelope's `to` DID. Lowercase kebab-case segments by convention; case-sensitive comparison.

name.description: Optional human-readable display name (e.g. `Paris cohort — dommage corporel`). For UI; not addressable.

description.description: Optional purpose statement for the channel. Free-form markdown.

creator.description: DID of the principal who created the channel. Must be the org owner or hold `admin` role at the org level.

createdAt.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp of channel creation.

visibility.description: Discoverability class. `public` = listed in the org's public-facing orgDoc and discoverable by anyone resolving the org's DID. `listed` = listed only to authenticated org members. `private` = not advertised in the orgDoc; existence shared out-of-band (e.g. via invite). All visibility classes still encrypt envelope bodies to channel members regardless — visibility governs *advertisement*, not *content*.

relayHint.description: Optional URL of the canonical relay endpoint for this channel. If absent, subscribers fall back to the org's default relay(s) listed in the parent orgDoc. Allows per-channel relay sovereignty (e.g. a high-sensitivity channel hosted on a dedicated relay).

parent.description: Optional handle of the parent channel (e.g. `dommage-corporel` for a leaf at `dommage-corporel:paris-cohort`). Redundant with the colon-path structure of `handle` itself; included only for indexing convenience. MAY be derived rather than persisted.

retiredAt.description: If present, the channel is retired (no new envelopes accepted) as of this timestamp. Retired channels remain readable; they don't disappear from history.

requires_stamp.description: Channel-governance policy (substrate-for-themia slice). When `true`, receivers MUST treat unstamped envelopes on this channel as *ambient* (informational), not authoritative; agents acting on received envelopes MUST NOT rely on signed-only traffic for authoritative interpretation. Channels carrying authoritative records (e.g. `assemblee_generale`, board decisions, contracts) set this. Default `false` (ambient channels — most traffic). Receiver-side discipline this slice; relay-side roster gating deferred per `[[role-tamper-proof]]`. See `docs/pitches/2026-05-21-substrate-for-themia.md` element §5.
